question: Does a class-balanced, cross-validated gradient-boosting pair classifier keep its similarity ranking better than a standard MLP pair classifier under an unseen optimisation profile?
method: Simulated opcode-count histograms (60 classes); same-source pairs from compiler profiles (substitution, dead code, renaming noise, drop/merge). Train on profiles A/B, test on unseen C.

dataset.name: Simulated compiled-procedure opcode histograms (numpy, profiles A/B train, C test)

metric_name: ROC-AUC on held-out profile C (main); F1@0.5 and log-loss (secondary)
baseline: Standardised MLPClassifier (128-64, early stopping) on pair features [|fa-fb|, fa*fb]
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM, 3-fold grouped-CV tuned (num_leaves, learning_rate), with added L1, cosine and training-normalised per-opcode count differences
notes: Simulated data, not real binaries; results are not comparable to the paper. Baseline has no tuning (paper gives no architecture). Test uses only the unseen profile C and procedures held out from training. Std is over 3 model seeds (ddof=0) on one fixed simulated dataset. Normalisation statistics come from training procedures under profiles A and B only.
